#include <bits/stdc++.h>

using namespace std;
#define int long long

const int maxn = 505;

int p;

int po(int a, int b) {
    if (b == 0) return 1;
    if (b == 1) return a;
    if (b % 2 == 0) {
        int u = po(a, b / 2);
        return (u * u) % p;
    } else {
        int u = po(a, b - 1);
        return (a * u) % p;
    }
}

int fact[maxn];
int invf[maxn];
int c3[maxn][maxn];

int c(int n, int k) {
    if (k < 0 || k > n) return 0;
    return c3[n][k];
}

int32_t main() {
    ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(0);
    cout.tie(0);
    
    int n, m;
    cin >> n >> m;
    cin >> p;
    
    // Precompute factorials and inverse factorials modulo p
    fact[0] = 1;
    for (int i = 1; i < maxn; ++i) {
        fact[i] = (fact[i-1] * i) % p;
    }
    
    // Compute modular inverse using Fermat's little theorem
    invf[maxn-1] = po(fact[maxn-1], p-2);
    for (int i = maxn-2; i >= 0; --i) {
        invf[i] = (invf[i+1] * (i+1)) % p;
    }
    
    // Precompute binomial coefficients
    for (int i = 0; i < maxn; ++i) {
        c3[i][0] = 1;
        for (int j = 1; j <= i; ++j) {
            c3[i][j] = (c3[i-1][j-1] + c3[i-1][j]) % p;
        }
    }
    
    // dp1[i] = number of valid arrangements for i computers
    // dp2[i] = sum of madeness for all valid arrangements of i computers
    int dp1[maxn] = {0};
    int dp2[maxn] = {0};
    
    dp1[0] = 1;
    dp2[0] = 0;
    
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < i; ++j) {
            // j computers on left, i-1-j computers on right
            int left = j;
            int right = i - 1 - j;
            
            dp1[i] = (dp1[i] + (dp1[left] * dp1[right]) % p * c(i-1, j)) % p;
            
            // Calculate contribution to madeness
            // When a new computer is added at position j+1 (0-indexed)
            // Left side has j computers, right side has right computers
            // The new computer is at position j+1 (1-indexed)
            
            // Madeness contribution from left subtree
            int left_madeness = dp2[left];
            // Madeness contribution from right subtree
            int right_madeness = dp2[right];
            
            // Additional madeness from participants sitting in left/right subtrees
            // Each participant in left subtree moves 1 extra step (to reach the new root)
            // Each participant in right subtree moves 1 extra step (to reach the new root)
            int extra_madeness = (dp1[left] * right % p + dp1[right] * left % p) % p;
            
            // Total madeness for this configuration
            int total_madeness = (left_madeness * dp1[right] % p + right_madeness * dp1[left] % p + extra_madeness) % p;
            
            dp2[i] = (dp2[i] + total_madeness * c(i-1, j)) % p;
        }
    }
    
    // dp3[i][j] = number of ways to arrange j participants on i computers
    // dp4[i][j] = sum of madeness for all valid arrangements of j participants on i computers
    int dp3[maxn][maxn] = {0};
    int dp4[maxn][maxn] = {0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) {
        dp3[i][0] = 1;  // 0 participants, 1 way (empty arrangement)
        dp4[i][0] = 0;
    }
    
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            for (int k = 0; k <= j; ++k) {
                // k participants sit on the left side of computer i
                // j-k participants sit on the right side of computer i
                // But actually, we need to consider the recursive structure differently
                
                // Let's reconsider: for computer i, participants can sit at positions 1..i
                // If the rightmost participant sits at position k+1 (0-indexed), then:
                // - k participants sit on computers 1..k
                // - j-k-1 participants sit on computers k+2..i
                
                if (k < j) {
                    dp3[i][j] = (dp3[i][j] + (dp3[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1]) % p * c(j, k)) % p;
                    dp4[i][j] = (dp4[i][j] + 
                                ((dp4[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1] % p + dp3[i-1][k] * dp2[j-k-1] % p) * c(j, k)) % p +
                                (dp3[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1] % p * (j-k-1)) % p) % p;
                } else {
                    dp3[i][j] = (dp3[i][j] + dp1[j]) % p;
                    dp4[i][j] = (dp4[i][j] + dp2[j]) % p;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Actually, let's use a cleaner approach based on the known solution pattern
    // The answer is: m! * 2^m * C(n+1, 2m) * (n - m + 1)
    
    // But let's compute it properly using the DP approach from known solutions
    
    // Reset DP arrays
    memset(dp3, 0, sizeof(dp3));
    memset(dp4, 0, sizeof(dp4));
    
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i) {
        dp3[i][0] = 1;
    }
    
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            for (int k = 0; k <= j; ++k) {
                if (k == j) {
                    dp3[i][j] = (dp3[i][j] + dp1[j]) % p;
                    dp4[i][j] = (dp4[i][j] + dp2[j]) % p;
                } else {
                    // k participants on left, j-k on right
                    dp3[i][j] = (dp3[i][j] + (dp3[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1] % p) * c(j, k)) % p;
                    dp4[i][j] = (dp4[i][j] + 
                                ((dp4[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1] % p + dp3[i-1][k] * dp2[j-k-1] % p) * c(j, k)) % p +
                                (dp3[i-1][k] * dp1[j-k-1] % p * (j - k - 1)) % p) % p;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    cout << (dp4[n][m] + p) % p;
    
    return 0;
}
